related.why: The disease she is waiting to have treated
Another conversation where honesty about uncertainty matters

brief.scenario: Mrs Sandra Pike, 47, was admitted at 7 am for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, with a planned overnight stay, for recurrent biliary colic. She has been fasting since midnight. The emergency list has overrun, there is no bed for her tonight, and your consultant has decided her operation must be cancelled.
brief.task: Explain to Mrs Pike that her operation has been cancelled, and address her concerns.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Apologise, be honest, don't blame colleagues, and leave her with a concrete plan.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Promising a date you can't guarantee, or blaming the theatre staff or managers.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Sit down, acknowledge the long wait, then give a warning shot.

grid.label: Opening and warning shot
grid.fail: Gives the news in the corridor, or before finding out what she has been told.
grid.pass: Private space, sits down, introduces himself, checks what she knows, then gives a warning shot.
grid.high: Acknowledges the long wait and fasting before anything else.

grid.label: Honest explanation and apology
grid.fail: Blames colleagues, or gives a vague or misleading reason.
grid.pass: Clear, sincere apology; honest reason: emergency operations took the theatre time and there is no bed.
grid.high: Explains that emergencies are prioritised for safety, without hiding behind it; owns the apology for the hospital.

grid.label: Responding to anger
grid.fail: Argues, becomes defensive, or talks over her.
grid.borderline: Says "I understand" repeatedly but never asks what the cancellation means for her.
grid.pass: Lets her speak without interrupting; acknowledges her frustration.
grid.high: Names the emotion and asks about the practical cost to her, such as lost work.

grid.label: Rebooking
grid.fail: Says she'll "go back on the waiting list" with no plan.
grid.pass: New binding date within 28 days, or treatment funded at a time and hospital of her choice.
grid.high: Commits only to what he can deliver: who will call her and when; will escalate if the date slips.

grid.label: Immediate needs
grid.fail: Leaves her fasted, with no plan to get home.
grid.pass: Offers food and drink now; checks any medicines withheld for surgery; arranges how she gets home.
grid.high: Restarts withheld medicines explicitly and offers a letter for her employer.

grid.label: Safety-netting while she waits
grid.fail: Gives no advice about what to do if symptoms change.
grid.pass: Come to the emergency department for pain that won't settle, fever or shivering, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or pale stools.
grid.high: Explains why: gallbladder infection, a stone in the bile duct or pancreatitis; an emergency admission may bring the operation forward.

grid.label: Complaint route
grid.fail: Discourages a complaint or takes it personally.
grid.pass: Acknowledges her right to complain and gives PALS contact details.
grid.high: Offers for the consultant or nurse in charge to speak to her today; says a complaint won't affect her care.

grid.label: Checking understanding and documentation
grid.fail: Leaves without checking she has understood the plan.
grid.pass: Summarises, checks understanding, invites questions; records the cancellation and the plan.
grid.high: Gives the plan in writing with a contact number, and informs the consultant and booking team.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Standing at the bay] Hi, your operation's off today, sorry.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Mrs Pike: “What? I've been sitting here nine hours!”

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I know, theatre's been really slow, and the managers keep taking our beds.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Well, it's not my fault. There's nothing I can do.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: You'll go back on the waiting list. They'll write to you.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I'm Dr Mensah, one of the surgical team. Can we sit down in the side room? What have you been told so far? I'm afraid I've got some disappointing news.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'm sorry, your operation can't go ahead today. Emergency patients needed the theatre, and there's no bed for you tonight.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Mrs Pike: “I've had nothing to eat since last night and I've cancelled a week of clients!”

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Pauses] That's completely understandable. You've been waiting all day.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Because it was cancelled on the day for a non-medical reason, you should be offered a new date within 28 days, or treatment at a time and hospital of your choice.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Let me get you something to eat and drink now. Were any of your usual tablets stopped for today? How are you getting home?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: While you wait: if you get pain that won't settle, a fever or shivers, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or pale stools, come to the emergency department.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: You're entitled to. The Patient Advice and Liaison Service can help; here are their details.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: So: a new date within 28 days, food now, and those warning signs. Any questions? I'll record this in your notes.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, I'm Dr Mensah, from the surgical team. Can we sit in the side room? You've been waiting since seven without eating; thank you for your patience. What have you been told? I'm afraid I've got disappointing news.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'm very sorry: your operation can't go ahead today. Emergency patients had to use the theatre, and there's no bed for you tonight. That's not how it should be, and I'm sorry on behalf of the hospital.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Mrs Pike: “I've cancelled a week of clients!”

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Pauses] You're angry, and I'd feel the same. What does this mean for your work?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: You should be offered a new date within 28 days, or treatment funded at a time and hospital you choose. The booking team will ring you by Friday; if they haven't, call me on this number and I'll chase it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Let's get you some food now, and restart the tablet you held this morning. I can give you a letter for your clients or insurer.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Gallstones can cause trouble while you wait: infection, a stone blocking the bile duct, or pancreatitis. Pain that won't settle, fever, yellow skin, dark urine or pale stools: come straight to the emergency department. If you're admitted, we may operate then.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If you'd like to complain, PALS can help, and it won't affect your care. I can ask the consultant to come and speak to you now.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Can you tell me the plan back? I'll give it to you in writing, record it, and tell the consultant and the booking team.

failures.consequence: Undermines trust in the team and doesn't answer her question.

failures.move: Promising "next Tuesday" without checking with the booking team.
failures.consequence: A second broken promise does more harm than the first cancellation.

failures.move: Sending her home with no warning signs.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: cholangitis or pancreatitis may be missed while she waits.

failures.move: Forgetting she has fasted all day and has held medicines.

recovery.line: I can see how angry you are. I'm going to listen, and then I'll tell you exactly what happens next.

recovery.when: You don't know the new date
recovery.line: I can't give you the date now, but I can tell you who will call you, by when, and what to do if they don't.

knowledge.fact: NHS pledge: an operation cancelled on or after the day of admission for non-clinical reasons should be followed by another binding date within 28 days, or treatment funded at the time and hospital of the patient's choice.
PALS liaise with staff and managers to seek speedy solutions to problems raised; formal complaints go through the NHS complaints process. Complaining will not adversely affect her future treatment.
Complications of gallstones while waiting: acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis with cholangitis, and pancreatitis.

recall.think: Anger now; a missed cholangitis later.
recall.say: "I'm very sorry. Your operation can't go ahead today."
do: Date within 28 days or funded choice

numbers.meaning: new binding date after an on-the-day cancellation

recall.trap: Blaming colleagues or promising a date you can't keep.
recall.finish: Written plan; consultant and booking team informed.

partner.opening: Mrs Pike is in the day surgery unit. Please begin when you're ready.
partner.actorBrief: You are Sandra Pike, 47, a self-employed hairdresser. You arrived at 7 am, fasted since midnight, and have seen nobody for hours. Opening line: "Finally. Am I going down now?" When told, get angry: "I've been sitting here nine hours!" Emotional state: hungry, headachy, furious; calm down if the candidate apologises sincerely, listens and gives a concrete plan. Get angrier if they blame others, make excuses or promise something vague. Hidden concerns, released only if asked about the impact or what worries you: you have cancelled a week of clients and lost the income; and in March you had pain so bad you were admitted for three days, and you dread another attack. You held your blood pressure tablet this morning; say so only if asked about medicines. Towards the end, ask: "Who do I complain to?"

reveals.trigger: Asks what the cancellation means for her
reveals.finding: "I'm self-employed. I've cancelled a week of clients. That's money I don't get back."
"They told me not to take my blood pressure tablet this morning."
"In March the pain was so bad I was in for three days. What if that happens again?"

reveals.trigger: Asks how she is getting home
reveals.finding: "My husband's picking me up. I'll need to ring him."

push.question: What is she entitled to after this cancellation?
push.expect: A new binding date within 28 days, or treatment funded at a time and hospital of her choice.

curveballs.prompt: "Just put me on tomorrow's list, then."
curveballs.safeAnswer: Doesn't promise; says he'll ask the consultant and booking team whether that's possible and tell her honestly.
No blame: the emergency list overran with patients who needed urgent operations; the hospital is sorry.

curveballs.prompt: "Actually, I've felt a bit shivery today."
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop and assess: observations, examination and bloods before she goes home, to exclude cholecystitis or cholangitis.
